title: Next.js Navigation Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on how the Next.js App Router navigates: soft vs hard navigation, prefetching, the navigation hooks, the client router cache and its staleness, redirect and notFound, and scroll and loading behaviour.

chapters.title: Navigation Mental Model
points: Soft navigation: client-side transition via <Link> or router.push; fetches the RSC payload only, keeps layouts mounted and preserves their state and client React state
Hard navigation: full document load (plain <a>, window.location, typing the URL, refresh); resets all client state and the router cache
Shared layouts do not re-render on soft navigation (partial rendering): only the segments below the changed one are fetched and rendered
Use <Link href> for internal routes: it is the primary navigation API and enables prefetching and client transitions
Navigation is wrapped in a React transition, so the old UI stays visible until the new one is ready or loading.js shows

chapters.title: Link Prefetching
points: <Link> prefetches when it enters the viewport, in production only (no prefetch in next dev)
Static routes: the full route payload is prefetched; dynamic routes: prefetch stops at the nearest loading.js boundary (shared layout down to the fallback)
prefetch={false} disables it; prefetch={true} also prefetches the full dynamic route (and caches it for longer)
router.prefetch('/path') prefetches programmatically, for example before a button-triggered router.push
Prefetching a dynamic page with no loading.js fetches little, so add loading.js to make instant navigation possible

chapters.title: Navigation Hooks
points: useRouter (next/navigation): push(url) adds a history entry, replace(url) overwrites it, back(), forward(), refresh(), prefetch(url); client components only
useRouter must come from next/navigation, not next/router, which is the Pages Router and throws in the App Router
usePathname returns the path only, with no query string, for example '/blog/1'; use it for active-link styling
useSearchParams returns a read-only URLSearchParams; update it by building a new string and calling router.push(`${pathname}?${params}`)
useSearchParams in a statically rendered route makes the client render bail out up to the nearest <Suspense> boundary, so wrap it in <Suspense> or the production build fails
These hooks are client-only: in server components use the page's searchParams prop (a Promise in recent versions, so await it), or params

chapters.title: Client Router Cache and Staleness
points: The router cache is an in-memory, per-session client cache of RSC payloads by route segment, separate from the server Data Cache and Full Route Cache
It is cleared on a hard refresh, and each tab has its own cache

Staleness window: dynamic pages are cached for 0s by default in recent versions (staleTimes.dynamic), static pages for 5 min; prefetch={true} keeps dynamic for 5 min; tune through experimental.staleTimes in next.config
router.refresh() re-fetches the current route from the server and keeps client state, but does not change the URL
Server actions that call revalidatePath/revalidateTag or cookies.set/delete invalidate the router cache, so the UI updates after a mutation
A stale page after a mutation made outside server actions (route handler, external API) means you must call router.refresh()

chapters.title: redirect, notFound, Scroll and Loading
points: redirect(url) from next/navigation: 307 by default (303 in server actions), works in server components, actions and route handlers; permanentRedirect gives 308
redirect and notFound work by throwing a special error, so never wrap them in try/catch (or call them after the try block); call it outside the catch or rethrow
In client components use useRouter().push for redirects; redirect() is only valid during render, not in event handlers
notFound() renders the nearest not-found.js with a 404 status; unmatched URLs fall through to the root not-found

Scroll: after navigation Next scrolls to the top of the new page, or to the first element of the segment if it is not in the viewport; <Link scroll={false}> and router.push(url, { scroll: false }) keep position
loading.js wraps the page in an automatic <Suspense> boundary, giving an instant fallback that streams the content in; it does not cover layouts
Navigation to the same route with changed search params does not re-run loading.js unless the Suspense key changes; add key={searchParams string} to a Suspense boundary

chapters.title: Navigation Cheat Sheet
points: <Link href>: soft navigation, prefetch in viewport (production only); prefetch={false} off; scroll={false} keeps scroll; replace swaps history entry
useRouter (next/navigation): push, replace, back, forward, refresh, prefetch; client only
usePathname gives the path; useSearchParams gives read-only URLSearchParams and needs a <Suspense> boundary
Server side: redirect (307/303), permanentRedirect (308), notFound (404), never inside try/catch
Router cache: dynamic 0s and static 5 min stale time by default; refresh with router.refresh() or revalidatePath/revalidateTag in a server action
Plain <a>, window.location and refresh are hard navigations that reset all client state
